images.title: From factors to the jump
images.purpose: Recap the method: list the factors of both treasure numbers, take the greatest common one, and that is the longest jump.
images.composition: Left half: two short rows of factor chips; right half: a small number line showing the chosen jump; a grey arrow links them.
exact_structure: Left: row 1 starts with the label 9 then exactly 3 teal (#0072B2) chips 1, 3, 9; row 2 starts with the label 15 then exactly 4 amber (#E69F00) chips 1, 3, 5, 15.
The chips 3 in both rows are filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) as the greatest common factor; the chips 1 have thin green (#009E73) circles.
A grey (#6B7280) arrow points from the chips to the right half.
Right: a number line from 0 to 15 with grey (#6B7280) ticks at every whole number; only 0, 9 and 15 labelled; reddish purple (#CC79A7) chests above 9 and 15.
Exactly 5 reddish purple (#CC79A7) arcs of length 3: 0 to 3, 3 to 6, 6 to 9, 9 to 12, 12 to 15, labelled jump of 3.
rejection: any count of arcs other than 5, or arcs not of length 3
a missing or extra factor in either chip row
any chip other than 3 filled as the greatest common factor
images.takeaway: The longest jump onto both treasures is the HCF, found by listing and comparing factors.
images.description: Factor chips for 9 and 15 with 3 highlighted, and a number line to 15 with five jumps of 3 landing on 9 and 15.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Use it as the recipe for the practice: factors, common factors, greatest, then check the jump on the line.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap linking factor lists to the jump helps before the practice items.
